title: Looking for better 3d Animation tools
author: SBelwas
selftext:
I am currently using a combination of Opus 5.5, blender and Meshy to make animations for the game im working on. Results have honestly been pretty bad, at least not to the standard im looking for. 

For context: I've been a software engineer for ~10 years but I am terrible at art. Coding has always been fine for me but the art... not so much. I've not worked on games in the past in part because the art part was always so hard and intimidating. I'd really like to see if anyone has some ai tools that can help me create the things i have in my mind.

comments.author: Illustrious-Pay6341
comments.body: Interesting! I am using Opus 5.5 with Blender MCP and my model come out amazing after few iteration. I usually do the sketching for the model instead of just prompting alone and once you define the colour you want, the first iteration might not be ok but then I provide feedback and it finishes the model how I want it to look like!

comments.author: Used-Snow-9934
comments.body:
If you want to make it great. Do some fundamental animation training to get an understanding what animation is, bouncing ball, some followthrough exercises, weight shift. Who knows you might even enjoy it more then you know. And that skill will help you with the procedural or generated animations later.  
You could use something like cascadeur to simplify things as well. Seems like a good way to direct animations with the help of ML and physics.

Not interested?  Look what motion capture can do for you, there are even markerless solutions now.  You just need a camera. I think UE has that built in now (at least for metahuman and faces,  you can transfer the animation later to your custom skeleton if you don’t want to use metahuman)

Generative AI can do a lot, it’s amazing, but chose the right tool for the right job.

comments.author: Brilliant_Ad2977
comments.body: I am struggling with the same thing. I used some animations from meshy but I am not very satisfied with transitions between animation. I am still searching for a solution and thinking about getting into it myself

comments.author: Psychological-Arm42
comments.body:
Directly saying “make it like this blah blah blah” didn’t work for me either. Instead you need to have a lot of stuff setup first.

Have a game design bible (GDD) and buildlog stored in your game folder always (and keep updating them, I use the graphify skill for this to save tokens) and ask the model to load the required parts into context upon each new chat. This way it always knows what the game is, and the design of the game, etc.

once you fix your game art direction, Theme , design and give it enough reference, It more or less knows what’s going to fit in the game. Since claude is notoriously bad at image gen. I use codex for it.

Ask claude to generate a big prompt, to paste into codex, for your required animations / VFX. Ask claude to direct codex to generate an offline chooser website, which generates sprite sheets of all the required animations at 24 fps. Ask it to make 2 or 3 choies for each animation. you can then see the animations at 24 fps and choose the ones u like, give the chosen files to claude, and claude can then add them to the game with good accuracy. It still requires some tweaking and refinement after claude makes it, but its what’s getting the job done for me
